title: Bounded Architecture Proof
problem: Consequential architecture choices can be overclaimed from a happy-path prototype, incomplete provider check, or template completion without exact stop criteria, adversarial evidence, cleanup, and non-proven implications.
invariant: An Architecture Proof supports only its exact hypothesis, subject version, environment, method, fixtures, and recorded result; unsupported and inconclusive outcomes remain valid evidence and never become production readiness by implication.
applicability_triggers: A consequential architecture claim has material feasibility uncertainty.
A risky dependency, provider, external-effect boundary, or large rationale package requires bounded proof.
A pattern may be promoted into shared Octon Mini guidance.
non_applicability_triggers: A routine reversible decision is already covered by ordinary validation and evidence.
The proposed proof has no decision-relevant hypothesis or stop condition.
exclusions: No mandatory proof artifact for every project decision.
No provider-specific fields in the common schema.
No inference from template completion or structural conformance to production readiness.
required_contracts: Exact hypothesis, subject, version, configuration, and environment.
Acceptance and stop criteria plus representative and adversarial cases.
Reproducible method, evidence, failures, skipped checks, cleanup or rollback, and limitations.
Supported, unsupported, or inconclusive conclusion and explicit non-proven implications.
prohibited_shortcuts: Treating a happy path as sufficient adversarial proof.
Using readiness-evidence proof kind to declare readiness without project-owned gates and current evidence.
Using a stale provider or dependency result for a changed exact subject.
failure_recovery_semantics: A stopped, failed, unsupported, or inconclusive proof preserves its evidence and limitations.
Cleanup or rollback failure is recorded as a residual effect, not hidden.
Changed subjects or environments require a new proof or explicit revalidation.
proof_expectations: Validate strict schema and semantic completion rules.
Exercise unsupported and inconclusive outcomes as legitimate results.
Reject missing stop criteria, inexact subjects, incomplete cleanup, absent limitations, and missing non-proof claims.
known_implementations: Octon Mini migration fixtures, reference evidence, and adversarial acceptance tests demonstrate the method internally without constituting generated project proof.

evidence.exact_subject: Project Blueprint 3.0.0 decision, evidence, migration, evaluation, and acceptance proof discipline
evidence.supports: One optional proof family closes the hypothesis, stop, adversarial, cleanup, and non-proof contract gap without adding default ceremony.
limitations: The new proof-family contract has not yet been adopted by two independent projects.

compatibility.migration_posture: Source-only optional schema and templates; no generated-project migration or profile inventory change.

migration.guidance: The source-only proof family is not copied into existing projects. A future generated-profile adoption requires separate taxonomy and migration analysis.

complexity: Adds proof authoring, fixture maintenance, and evidence retention when deliberately used.
operator_burden: Consequential proofs require exact environments, adversarial cases, and truthful cleanup reporting.

status_history.rationale: Allocated for architecture review as one consolidated proof family.
Schema and source templates accepted; generated-profile adoption remains explicitly excluded.

limitations: The proof family is source-only and optional.
A proof record cannot grant authority, accept a decision, or establish production readiness by itself.
